page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No margin notes. Page number at top right. Running head at top centre. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: 4. Quòd si illis duobus, Legi inquam fidei & operum, respodeat intentio, tum demum bona cenferi debet.
Ratio manifesta est: Quia mens luce Dei fulgens, & voluntas à Spiritu sancto ducta, utitur ministerio inferiorum viriũ ad Dei obsequium, qui ultimus est bonæ intentionis finis.

5. Neq; verò ab horum ordine, heroici & ardentis Spiritus opera seiungi debet: etsi nostrum non est, sine speciali mandato ea imitari. Notum est illud de Phineës, Psal. 106. 30. Sed adfuit Phinees, & vin dicauit (scelus,) & cohibita est plaga.
31. Et imputatū est ei ad iusticiam, in gene[?] ratione & generatione usq; in seculum.

6. Cætera non nisi ἰμωνύμως loquendo, bona intētione fieri aut omitti dicimus, cum factorum species diuersæ sunt ab ijs quæ præcepit Dominus: ut ἰϑελοϑρησκείαι [?] Baalitarum & monachorum: vel cum alij modi & fines sunt actionum & omissionum, quàm Deus velit & præceperit.
Prioris ordinis olim erant victimæ hū mānæ, Molech aut Saturno oblatæ, [illegible, ~6 letters]- φιλίᾳ [?] quadam Abrahæ ductis idololatris, ut Deo exsecrabilem cultum præstarent.

page.notes: Printed text is in a single column; the first line is numbered "4." and starts a new paragraph, so no cont marker. "31." begins a new line after a short line ending "plaga.", and is treated as a new paragraph; this is uncertain. "in gene ratione & generatione" is hard to resolve (possibly a split word); the first "gene" is marked [?]. The Greek words "ἰμωνύμως" and "ἰϑελοϑρησκείαι" are copied approximately and are doubtful; the Greek after "oblatæ" is doubtful as well. The signature "i" at the left foot and the catchword "Ad po-" at the right foot were read from the scan. Some letters in the first lines (e.g. "respodeat", "cenferi") are printed as seen, including printing errors. "uin dicauit" printed as "vin dicauit".
